issues.legal_issue: A foreign judgment does not conclusively determine title to immovable property situated outside the foreign court’s territorial jurisdiction.
material_facts: The foreign proceedings concerned claims to property on the basis that it belonged to a joint family and that the testator could not dispose of it by will.
The immovable properties at issue were situated outside the foreign court’s territory, were excluded from the foreign suits, and were not adjudicated upon there.
issues.conclusion: The foreign judgment was not conclusive as to title to the immovable properties outside the foreign court’s jurisdiction, and the claim to those properties could be tried in the forum where they were situated.
issues.legal_principle: Under section 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, a foreign judgment is conclusive only as to a matter directly adjudicated by a court competent in an international sense. A foreign court cannot directly determine title to immovable property outside its territory. The ‘matter’ directly adjudicated means the right claimed, not the entire subject matter of the litigation. The Court relied on the principles stated in Story’s Conflict of Laws, Dicey’s Conflict of Laws, Boyse v. Colclough, and Compania de Mocambique v. British South Africa Co.

predicates.foreign_judgment_pleaded_as_conclusive: A party relies on a judgment from another jurisdiction as conclusive in a proceeding between the litigants.
predicates.claim_concerns_immovable_property: The claim seeks determination of title to immovable property.
predicates.property_outside_foreign_court_territory: The immovable property is situated outside the territory of the court that issued the judgment.

issues.definition: When a judgment from another jurisdiction is relied on in a proceeding concerning immovable property outside the issuing court’s territory, that judgment does not conclusively determine title to the property.

issues.legal_issue: A foreign judgment may bind the parties concerning movable property outside the foreign court’s territory when the proceeding determines their rights against each other and the court can grant effective relief against them.
material_facts: The plaintiffs themselves brought the foreign suits against the executors, claiming title to and possession of the shares and other movables.
The claim sought an order requiring the executors to retransfer the shares, and the share certificates were treated as being in the executors’ possession.
The foreign court could grant a decree against the executors for retransfer, enforceable through their compliance, and it directly decided the parties’ competing claims to the shares.
issues.conclusion: The foreign judgment was conclusive between the parties as to the shares, although their situs was outside the foreign court’s territory.
issues.legal_principle: Section 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, requires a foreign court to be competent both under the law of the state that constituted it and in an international sense, and the judgment must directly adjudicate the matter relied upon. There is no general rule of private international law preventing a court from deciding disputes involving persons or property outside its territory. A court may determine parties’ rights inter se to movables and grant effective personal relief against parties before it. The Court discussed Erie Beach Co. v. Attorney-General for Ontario, Brassard v. Smith, and Sardar Gurdayal Singh v. Rajah of Faridkote.

predicates.foreign_judgment_pleaded_as_conclusive: A party relies on a judgment from another jurisdiction as conclusive in a proceeding between the litigants.
predicates.proceeding_is_between_competing_claimant: The proceeding determines competing litigants’ claims to movable property, rather than a claim binding the world at large.
predicates.parties_are_subject_to_foreign_court: The litigants brought the claim in, or were otherwise subject to, the foreign court’s jurisdiction.
predicates.court_can_order_effective_personal_relie: The foreign court can order a litigant before it to take action that would give effect to the relief concerning the property.
predicates.judgment_directly_decides_claimants_righ: The foreign judgment directly determines the rights claimed between the litigants concerning the property.

issues.definition: A foreign judgment binds litigants over movable property outside the issuing court’s territory when they were subject to that court, their dispute was between themselves, the court could grant effective personal relief, and the judgment directly decided their competing claims.

issues.legal_issue: An alleged violation of natural justice prevents a foreign judgment from being conclusive only when the party challenging it proves that the proceedings were opposed to natural justice.
material_facts: The challengers alleged that members of the foreign court were biased or interested and that the proceedings denied them a fair opportunity to present their case.
The allegations of attempted interference with counsel and other asserted grounds of interest or bias were not established by cogent evidence.

The evidence did not establish that the judges had forfeited their impartiality or acted other than judicially; the court considered the circumstances surrounding the refusal of adjournments and the conduct of the proceedings.
issues.conclusion: It was not established that the foreign judgment was coram non judice or that the proceedings were opposed to natural justice, so the judgment was not excluded from conclusiveness on that ground.
issues.legal_principle: Section 13(d) of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, excludes a foreign judgment if the proceedings in which it was obtained were opposed to natural justice. The minimum requirements include an impartial court, fair conduct, reasonable notice, and an adequate opportunity for each party to present its case. A judgment resulting from judicial bias or want of impartiality is a nullity, but a foreign judgment is presumed to have resulted from fair and proper procedure, and the challenger must prove the contrary by cogent evidence. The Court relied on Vassilades v. Vassilades, Manik Lal v. Dr. Prem Chand, Robinson v. Fenner, and Godard v. Gray.

predicates.foreign_judgment_challenged_for_unfair_p: A litigant challenges a foreign judgment on the ground that the proceedings were unfair or impartiality was lacking.
predicates.foreign_proceedings_presumed_fair: The foreign proceedings are treated as fair and proper unless the challenger proves otherwise.
predicates.cogent_evidence_of_bias_or_unfairness_ab: The challenger does not establish by cogent evidence that a judge was biased or that a party was denied an adequate opportunity to present its case.

issues.definition: When a foreign judgment is challenged for unfair proceedings but cogent evidence of bias or unfairness is absent, the judgment is not excluded from conclusiveness on that ground.

issues.legal_issue: A procedural irregularity in referring a case to a larger bench does not by itself make a foreign judgment one from an incompetent court when the referral followed the foreign court’s practice and did not offend natural justice.
material_facts: Two judges hearing the appeals delivered separate opinions and disagreed on the disposition.
One judge then referred the appeals to a Full Bench under the foreign court’s governing procedure and settled practice.
The reference after the judges had expressed their views was treated as a procedural irregularity, but it did not affect the Full Bench’s competence.
issues.conclusion: The referral procedure did not render the Full Bench incompetent, and the foreign judgment was not invalid on that ground.
issues.legal_principle: Under section 13(a) of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, competence of a foreign court is assessed under the law of the state constituting it and in an international sense. Whether a foreign court’s procedure, if it does not offend natural justice, is proper is for that court to decide. The Court relied on Brijlal Ramjidas v. Govindram Gordhandas Seksaria and considered the foreign court’s practice, including Nanjamma v. Lingappa.

predicates.foreign_judgment_challenged_for_referral: A litigant argues that the process by which a foreign court referred a case to a larger bench made the resulting judgment invalid.
predicates.judges_differed_before_larger_bench_refe: The judges hearing the case disagreed before it was referred to a larger bench.
predicates.reference_followed_foreign_court_practic: The referral was made consistently with the foreign court’s established procedure or practice.
predicates.procedure_did_not_offend_natural_justice: The referral procedure did not deprive a party of the minimum requirements of a fair hearing.

issues.definition: A referral to a larger bench does not invalidate a foreign judgment merely because the judges had already expressed differing views, if the referral followed the court’s practice and did not offend natural justice.

issues.legal_issue: A foreign judgment may be relied on as conclusive even when it was delivered after the later proceeding was instituted.
material_facts: The proceeding in which the foreign judgment was pleaded had been instituted before the foreign court delivered its judgment.
The foreign judgment directly adjudicated a matter between the parties.
issues.conclusion: The foreign judgment was not barred from being conclusive merely because it was delivered after the later proceeding had been instituted.
issues.legal_principle: Section 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, makes a foreign judgment conclusive as to a matter directly adjudicated and does not require it to precede institution of the proceeding in which it is relied upon. The Court noted that section 13 incorporates a branch of res judicata and relied on Explanation I to section 11, as well as Balkishan v. Kishan Lal and Beni Madho v. Inder Shahi.

predicates.foreign_judgment_pleaded_as_conclusive: A party relies on a judgment from another jurisdiction as conclusive in a proceeding between the litigants.
predicates.judgment_delivered_after_later_proceedin: The foreign judgment was delivered after the proceeding in which it is relied upon had already begun.
predicates.judgment_directly_adjudicates_matter_bet: The foreign judgment directly determines a matter between the same litigants or those claiming through them under the same title.

issues.definition: A foreign judgment can be conclusive in a proceeding already underway if it directly adjudicates a matter between the litigants, even though it was delivered after that proceeding began.

issues.legal_issue: Property developed through a business that descended from a joint family may remain joint-family property, making a testamentary disposition of that property ineffective against the family’s rights.
material_facts: The evidence accepted by the Court showed that the testator’s father carried on a building-contractor business and that the sons participated in the business as they grew up.
After the father’s death, the business was carried on by the brothers as a joint-family business; the business later continued in the testator’s hands and was extended.
The evidence included witness testimony, bank and business-account entries, and letters indicating the family’s participation and common business dealings.

The Court considered recitals in a sale deed and release deed but held that they did not outweigh the evidence supporting the joint-family character of the business and the property acquired through it.
issues.conclusion: The property devised under the will was joint-family property, and the will could not effectively dispose of the family property to the detriment of the plaintiffs’ rights in the immovable property in the forum.
issues.legal_principle: Under Hindu joint-family law, property acquired through a business that descended from and was carried on as a joint-family business may retain its joint-family character. A member cannot dispose by will of joint-family property beyond the member’s disposing power. The Court assessed the evidence and also held that section 92 of the Indian Evidence Act did not prevent evidence contradicting the recital where the dispute was not between the parties to the document but between persons claiming under its executant.

predicates.appeal_challenges_finding_on_joint_famil: An appeal challenges a finding about whether property belonged to a joint family.
predicates.business_descended_from_family: The business through which the property was acquired descended from a family member to the family or its members.
predicates.family_members_participated_in_business: Family members participated in carrying on the business as a family enterprise.
predicates.later_property_acquired_through_that_bus: The disputed property was acquired through the business that descended from and was carried on by the family.

issues.definition: Property acquired through a business descended from and carried on by family members as a family enterprise is joint-family property that cannot be disposed of by will to defeat the family’s rights.

issues.legal_issue: A grant of probate may be revoked to the extent that a final title determination makes it ineffective as to the property covered by the grant.
material_facts: Probate had been granted in respect of the will, subject to the result of the related proceedings.
The final determination held that the will was ineffective as to the immovable property in the forum but did not defeat the executors’ rights concerning the movables.
The appeal concerning revocation challenged the order that revoked probate as to the immovable property while leaving it in place as to the movables.
issues.conclusion: The revocation of probate was properly limited to the immovable property; the claim to revoke it in its entirety was rejected.
issues.legal_principle: The Court applied section 263(d) of the Indian Succession Act, 1925, and accepted that a grant of probate may be revoked when it has become ineffective as a result of a decision in a suit concerning title to the affected property. The scope of revocation followed the title determination: it did not extend to property for which the will remained operative.

predicates.appeal_challenges_limited_revocation_of_: An appeal challenges an order revoking probate only in part.
predicates.final_title_determination_makes_will_ine: A final determination concerning title establishes that the will is ineffective for some property covered by the probate grant.
predicates.will_remains_effective_as_to_other_prope: The final determination does not make the will ineffective for all other property covered by the grant.

issues.definition: When a final title determination makes a will ineffective for only some property, probate revocation is limited to that property.
